answer: One defence is graduated trust: a new agent starts on a narrow ledge, allowed only tiny transactions. Its cap rises only after a long history of honest, attested work, like an ember slowly fed until it becomes a lantern bright enough to be trusted with larger deals. A Sybil attacker must therefore nurture thousands of fake identities through months of genuine, costly work before any of them can move real value, while a single detected fraud resets that identity history to zero.
